insight.title: Why Subscriptions Make Products Worse
insight.subtitle: Once a company secures your monthly payment, their goal shifts from exciting you to making it too painful to leave.

sections.text: When you buy a product once, the company has to delight you to get your cash. But once you subscribe, the developer’s main goal shifts from making you happy to keeping you locked in.

Instead of building exciting new features, they focus on lock-in—making it incredibly tedious to export your data, change your habits, or migrate to a competitor. They invest in friction, not innovation.

This is why subscription software often feels bloated and stagnant. The business model incentivizes captive audiences over satisfied customers, turning your favorite tools into digital landlords that demand rent without doing repairs.
Once they have your subscription, they invest in handcuffs, not features.
